mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods following a sustained increase in HOUST over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions or a slowdown in manufacturing, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a quarter, it signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where RSAFS growth exceeded CPIAUCSL growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment reacts quickly to employment data.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS decreased by more than 100,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above the historical average and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it signals a restrictive monetary policy during an economic contraction, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > historical average AND GDPC1 growth < 0%
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above the historical average and GDPC1 growth was negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over three months signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases AND UNRATE decreases over 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where HOUST increased and UNRATE decreased.
